News

Manga Creator Yū Asai Dies, Manga Creator Husband Motoyuki Asai Hospitalized After Traffic Accident

posted on by Crystalyn Hodgkins

A funeral for Yū was held by close family members.

Manga creator Ken Akamatsu (Love Hina) stated on Twitter on Friday that Motoyuki had suffered a stroke in 2015, and after Yū requested support at that time, Akamatsu had been working with them ever since. He expressed his condolences and added Motoyuki's rehabilitation after the stroke had been going well before the accident.

Motoyuki was the assistant to Game Center Arashi manga creator Mitsuru Sugaya. He debuted as a manga creator in 1984 with the Magnum Taishō manga in a special issue of Coro Coro Comics magazine. One year later he launched the Famicom Rocky manga (pictured at right) in the same magazine. He also drew the Sukebō Rocky manga.

Yū was a former assistant of Motoyuki's. The two worked together on manga under Yū's name. Yū is known for the Hoshi no Kazu dake Dakishimete, Kimagure Short Cut, Kakeru-kun Wake up!!, and Lovin' You manga, which were published in the 1990s.

is a Japanese manga artist and the creator of the series One Piece, the best-selling manga in history and the best-selling comic series printed in volume. With more than 520 million copies of One Piece in circulation worldwide, Oda is one of the best-selling fiction authors. The series' popularity resulted in Oda being named one of the artists who changed the history of manga.

Early life

Eiichiro Oda was born on January 1, 1975, in Kumamoto, Japan. At the age of four he resolved to become a manga artist in order to avoid having to get a "real job". His biggest influence was Akira Toriyama and his series Dragon Ball. He recalls that his interest in pirates was probably sparked by the popular TV animation series titled Vicky the Viking.

Career

At the age of 17, Oda submitted his work Wanted! and won several awards, including second place in the coveted Tezuka Award. Interest

One Manga Author is Teaching His Craft to Prisoners

posted on by Lynzee Loveridge

Manga author Ryō Sonoba is taking a step away from his work as a mystery manga artist to create an essay about his recent work in Japanese prisons. His non-fictional work Keimusho de Manga o Oshiete Imasu. (I'm Teaching Manga in Prison) details his experience teaching inmates how to draw manga at the Mine Rehabilitation Program Center in Yamaguchi prefecture.

Some of the inmates' work has appeared as background images in Sonoba's published manga, like Asami Mitsuhiko Mystery Special #23: Yogore Chimatta Michi. Other images drawn by Sonoba's students can be purchased for use at the website Mangaka Honpo.

Mine Rehabilitation Program Center is a short-term facility that houses first-offense inmates with low risk of recidivism. The center's web page explains that the manga background drawing program is thought to help with social reintegration and "cultivate perseverance and concentration."

Sonoba launched the new manga in the June issue of Monthly Comic Flapper on May 2. Sonoba wrote on Twitter that he would like to continue to draw his interactions with inmates as long as possible, with permission from the Ministry of Justice.

Source: Comic Natalie

results.snippet:

---
title: Akiko Higashimura and the art of shoujo manga writing
author: Seiko
date: 2017-12-20
---
Higashimura Akiko is in many ways an exceptional mangaka. You can catch a glimpse of it from her recent success with Princess Jellyfish and Tokyo Tarareba Girls, but there's so much more to be told about this hitmaker.

Although her exposure to the western fandom is fairly recent, Higashimura is a veteran with nearly 20 years of experience and has published over 90 comics across multiple genres. It may also surprise you to learn that this shoujo manga author has always had difficulty writing romance, and that her breakthrough hit was in fact not a shoujo romance but a hilarious manga essay about her motherhood.

Equally little-known is that, for over ten years, she's been running multiple serializations simultaneously, outputting a total of about 100 pages every month with the help of her assistants. A 2,000-word article is not enough to cover the entirety of this powerhouse mangaka's career, but you may find something new in here about her earlier key works and their significance, as well as her working style and a recent controversy surrounding her mangaka-assistant relationship.

Enter the Half-Dragon

High schooler Ruri Aoki wakes up one day to find she grew a pair of horns overnight. The most surprising thing is how unsurprised Ruri's mother seems, and Ruri soon finds out why: Ruri's biological father is a dragon!

Ruri tries to go about her day as normal, but that flies out the window when flames start flying out of her mouth. It sounds like this would be the start of a heroic adventure, but Ruri's human throat doesn't appreciate being burned to a crisp.

Learning that her human body will have to adjust to each new dragon trait as they appear, Ruri tries to live a normal life while suffering the growing pains of half-dragon puberty.

RuriDragon

Writing and Art by Masaoki Shindo

Published by Shueisha, Viz Media

Serialized in Weekly Shonen Jump, Shonen Jump+

Running since June 13, 2022

Appropriate for ages 13 and up

While family-friendly series geared toward younger audiences often receive plenty of fanfare, their more mature counterparts frequently go unappreciated thanks to their dark subject matter and graphic violence. Competition is often the engine for all personal successes, allowing us to see how far we can really go

When Shueisha, a Japanese publishing company, launched Shonen Jump on August 1st, 1968, the aim was to compete with the other two most popular magazines of the time: Weekly Shonen Sunday and Weekly Shonen Magazine. Initially launched on a bi-weekly basis, Shonen Jump would come out weekly and become one of the most important Japanese cultural phenomena ever.

Tracing the history, influence, and success of Shonen Jump is one of the leitmotifs behind Sabukaru, which explores the foundations of the modern community in all its socio-cultural aspects. Above all, the manga phenomenon has defined and narrated the canons of a troubled society, but one full of creative minds.

"When Shōnen Jump (renamed as Weekly Shōnen Jump afterward) was launched by Shueisha in 1968, it was only a magazine targeted at boys in primary school. But after making a couple of issues, we found that adults needed shōnen manga as much as the young boys. We thus changed to publish manga that was more sophisticated," said Hiroki Goto, one of the first and most important editors of Shonen Jump.

Umi Kusahara

Glacier Bay Books

April 2023

Mothers, released by Glacier Bay Books after a successful Kickstarter campaign, collects twelve stories about small but significant moments of kindness enacted in uncommon ways. Umi Kusahara's short stories are accented by touches of the fantastic but grounded in a reality that doesn't pull its punches. These stories are particularly concerned with grieving and the emotional impact of loss, which is represented delicately but without sentimentality.

In the piece that lends its title to the collection, "Mothers," two women visit the hospital beds of two teenagers who have only barely survived a horrible car crash. Each woman has a complicated relationship with the patient she visits, but they find sympathy and support in the connection they create with each other. As in the other stories in the collection, the catharsis lies in the moment of clarity when the characters can be finally honest with themselves about what they want and what will make their lives worth living.

One Manga Author is Teaching His Craft to Prisoners

posted on by Lynzee Loveridge

Manga author Ryō Sonoba is taking a step away from his work as a mystery manga artist to create an essay about his recent work in Japanese prisons. His non-fictional work Keimusho de Manga o Oshiete Imasu. (I'm Teaching Manga in Prison) details his experience teaching inmates how to draw manga at the Mine Rehabilitation Program Center in Yamaguchi prefecture.

Some of the inmates' work has appeared as background images in Sonoba's published manga, like Asami Mitsuhiko Mystery Special #23: Yogore Chimatta Michi. Other images drawn by Sonoba's students can be purchased for use at the website Mangaka Honpo.

Mine Rehabilitation Program Center is a short-term facility that houses first-offense inmates with low risk of recidivism. The center's web page explains that the manga background drawing program is thought to help with social reintegration and "cultivate perseverance and concentration."

Sonoba launched the new manga in the June issue of Monthly Comic Flapper on May 2. Sonoba wrote on Twitter that he would like to continue to draw his interactions with inmates as long as possible, with permission from the Ministry of Justice.

Spy × Family is a Japanese manga series written and illustrated by Tatsuya Endo. The series began serialization on the manga website Shōnen Jump+ on March 25, 2019. Its individual chapters have been collected in 15 tankōbon volumes, with the first having been released on July 4, 2019. The series is licensed for English-language release in North America by Viz Media, who published the first volume on June 2, 2020. As the series is published in Japan, it is also released simultaneously in English digitally on Viz Media's website.

The covers of the tankōbon features a main character resting on a designer's chair, surrounded by item(s) or characteristics that represent the character, their life and their personalities. The real life chairs were chosen by the author as he deemed fit with the character's personalities. For volume 10, Endo decides to forgo the inclusion of the designer chair motif to make the cover befit the volume's story.

──When did you become Tatsuya Endo's editor?

He takes the role of the main protagonist in the Yorknew City and Succession Contest arcs. He was also the deuteragonist of the Hunter Exam arc.

Appearance[]

Kurapika has medium blond hair with brown eyes; blue in the 1999 anime adaptation (grey/dark grey in the 2011 anime adaptation). His eyes glow a beautiful and coveted scarlet when experiencing intense emotion. In his first appearance in the series, he wears a blue tabard decorated with an orange-colored (red in the 2011 anime adaptation) hem and a white full-body training suit underneath. He changes his tabard and training suit for the duration of the Yorknew City arc. His shoes are Chinese-style winkle-picker flats. Chainsaw Man is Tatsuki Fujimoto's most famous ongoing work, although with other acclaimed projects before and since then, including Fire Punch, Goodbye, Eri, and Look Back (recently adapted into a successful anime movie) he's amassed an adoring following. However, Fujimoto's work has not only shaped the readers' perception of his idiosyncratic style over the years, but also the careers of many other mangaka. The Chainsaw Man creator had incredible assistants behind him, including Tatsuya Endo, Oto Tōda, Yuji Kaku, Yukinobu Tatsu, and Tohru Kuramori.

Chainsaw Man has become a global phenomenon, selling over 28 million copies. Fujimoto's many assistants have also gone on to create stories and attain impressive presences in the manga scene, with massive hit anime to many of their credit. While this is not an unusual phenomenon, the impressive number of assistants to Tatsuki Fujimoto who have gone on to create other successful manga is fascinating to explore.

A Day in the Limelight
---
title: A Day in the Limelight
date: 2007-02-12
---
A secondary or Ensemble character gets the primary focus for an episode in an atypical fashion. This can be used to either give various cast members a rest, both for the actor and for the audience or to allow different episodes to be shot simultaneously to save on time or costs. It can also be used to explore the possibility of an expanded role for a recurring or secondary character, or to set up a Spin-Off. Fans of secondary characters may explore the idea of their favourite character becoming the primary protagonist in a Fanfic.

Sometimes the limelight is given to a guest character of note, often a character so outrageous that they upstage the regulars, or a nobody with a touching, moving story. This is occasionally done in comedies where the focus is less on the regular characters usual antics and hijinks, and more on the guest character. In such cases, the regular characters may be temporarily demoted to Straight Man status. In some cases, the regular characters are just present either to provide moral support or to be the recipients of An Aesop. Such episodes may be of the Very Special Episode variety and may focus on a serious issue facing the guest character.

While often times this trope only applies to secondary or background characters, in an ensemble cast with fairly equitable time sharing, any episode that shines the spotlight on one particular character can be considered a Limelight Ep

Cruise Adventure Arc
---
title: Cruise Adventure Arc
---
| " | The world is soiled with needless tragedies. To prevent just one of them from befalling him or anyone else... takes thorough cleaning. And that still hasn't changed. In fact... now it's more true than ever. I don't need to be at peace. I don't care if I have to bloody my hands. Even if it means living a life that could end at any moment... Even if it means having to leave the Forger family... I think Loid would respect that. He would understand. That's why I won't give up this fight! | " |

Note that the following sub-headings are fan-made and used to better organize the story.

The Cruise Adventure Arc is the tenth story arc in SPY x FAMILY. In the anime adaptation, the arc is referred as the Luxury Cruise Ship Arc (

The assassin Thorn Princess receives a mission to protect Olka Gretcher and her son from a group of skilled assassins aboard the Princess Lorelei cruise ship. However, when Loid and Anya coincidentally board the same ship thanks to a giveaway they won, Yor begins to have doubts about her life as an assassin.

Summary[]

The Informant's Romance Endeavors[]

Loid visits Franky's store to pick up some items for an extra mission. Loid asks for some pictures he requested, but Franky says his contact that specialized in that intel got done in by Garden, an assassin group in Ostania that takes orders from the shadow government and is believed to be urban legends. Loid still requests the pictures, but Franky wants his help for a job in exchange for the extra trouble: finding a missing cat. Franky explains that the cat, Kopi, belongs to a girl he is trying to court. Completely uninterested, Loid turns him down. Franky turns to his contacts to find Kopi's location, which is near city hall, and on his way there, he runs into Yor, who is out on her lunch break.

After Franky explains his situation, Yor decides to help him out. Franky sets up several of his own inventions to locate Kopi and uses a catnip device to lure in the feline. However, the device draws in a large crowd of cats that swarm Yor and Franky, but Kopi is spotted among them. Franky tries to catch Kopi but fails, and he decides to use his exo-skeleton power suit. But when Kopi starts heading to a major street, Yor tears off a chunk of the exo-skeleton and throws it at the cat, stopping it in its tracks and allowing Yor to capture him. While he lost ten years of his work, Franky returns Kopi only to learn that the girl already has a boyfriend. Yor returns to work at city hall, and Director Matthew McMahon informs Yor that she has a call from her "special contact." Answering the phone, the Thorn Princess receives a new "client."[2]

Thorn Princess's New Assignment[]

Yor and Matthew head to a luxurious garden maintained by the Shopkeeper. Yor and the Shopkeeper briefly chat before the Shopkeeper suddenly attacks her, wanting to test if her skills have dulled. Yor swiftly dodges the attack, and the Shopkeeper comfortably assigns her a new job to protect her client. The Shopkeeper explains that the Gretcher mob family, who have managed Ostania's underworld, has recently lost their patriarch and his sons in an internal dispute, with only his daughter, Olka Gretcher, and her son as the sole survivors. The new leader of the organization, Leonardo Hapoon, has put an enormous bounty on the mother and son's heads that almost every hitman in and out of the country is out for them. Because the Shopkeeper owes a debt to the previous boss, he has chosen to assist Olka, deciding that seeking asylum in a foreign country is her best option. She will do this by fleeing by sea, traveling on a normal passenger ship, and later rendezvous with another at the port of disembarkation.

Yor's assignment is to protect Olka and her son from the assassins and act as a backup in case something goes wrong. Yor is hesitant as she worries about her cover at work and home. However, Garden has already prepared a cover story that she is there as part of her work. With her mind at rest, the Thorn Princess gladly accepts the assignment. On her way home, Yor encounters Yuri, and she begins to wonder with him now grown up and independent of her if there is a point in keeping her assassin job.

Meanwhile, Loid and Anya are at the mall when they see a raffle with a grand prize of two tickets for a three-day, two-night cruise on a ship named Princess Lorelei, which sails through the islands in Ostanian coastal waters. Excited, Anya is determined to go on the trip and participates in the raffle. She soon realizes that the host has rigged the raffle for himself, so she takes the winning tickets. When Yor returns home, Anya shows her the tickets, and Loid suggests that Yor and Anya go on the cruise together since he has work. However, Yor recognizes it as the same ship she will be on for her job. Anya reads her mind and, after some thought, insists on going on the trip. Loid then goes to Sylvia to ask for time off, and, to his surprise, she allows him to go and tells him to consider the trip as part of Anya's care and education for Operation Strix, treating it like any other mission.

On the Friday of the departure, the Forgers head to the port, leaving Bond at home with Franky. On their way there, Yor wishes she could spend her time with Loid and Anya, and wonders if she could make this trip her final job as the Thorn Princess. Upon reaching Princess Lorelei, the family split up as suspicious figures also board the ship.[3]

The Assassin Ambush[]

Inside Princess Lorelei, Anya is amazed by the many activities the boat offers, but not so much for their third-class suite. Meanwhile, Yor and the city hall group meet with Olka, who has disguised herself as "Shaty Grey," alongside her ally and acting husband, "Furseal." As the rest of the group tours around the ship, Yor stays behind with Olka. The women talk, and Yor learns about Olka's desire to live a quiet life with her son, away from power and money. Olka requests to go outside for a moment, but Yor is reluctant since Loid and Anya are also on the ship. On the lower suite, Loid and Anya explore the ship. Loid finds himself falling back to "Twilight mode" and is determined to attain optimal recreation.

Yor explains her family situation to Olka, who questions if the family really is just for her cover. Olka lends Yor her clothes as a disguise, and they head outside with Olka's son. Yor empathizes with Olka's circumstances and promises to finish the job without fail. Touched, Olka reveals her son's name to Yor, Gram. Their conversation is heard on a listening device, and an informant uses this information to locate Olka's cabin room.[4]

At nighttime, Yor's co-workers have dinner at a pub and talk about Yor's trip. On the ship, the city hall group and the Grey family eat at a fancy restaurant. Afterward, the men leave for a bar while Yor and Olka head back to the cabin. There, Olka notes there has not been any sign of trouble the entire day, but Yor warns her that they must keep their guard up as they have no idea where the enemy is or what their plan is. She predicts that the enemy will try attacking at the last possible minute, which will be the next day. Olka asks what everyone else will do if she manages to escape safely, and Yor explains their prepared cover story. Olka then asks if Yor will see her family after she completes her mission, as the ship will stop at a resort island on the third day. She suggests that Yor could use it to spend time with her family, but Yor is unsure.

On the lower deck, Loid and Anya have their dinner and take note of how strange it is to have dinner without Yor, which leads to Loid getting embarrassed when Anya calls him sappy for missing Yor. Meanwhile, after leaving the bar with the other men, Matthew notices they are being followed. He ambushes their stalker and interrogates him for information. Upon learning there are many assassins on board the ship and know Olka's location, Matthew grabs Furseal and rushes back to her cabin, realizing that the enemy had no intention of waiting.

At the cabin, the women hear someone knock on the door.[5] Behind it is an assassin who immediately attacks, but Yor kills him shortly after Matthew and Furseal arrive. Matthew brings everyone up to speed with their situation and orders Yor to take the others to another cabin in the second-class suite, but not before giving everyone masks to disguise themselves. The informant from earlier informs a group of assassins that "Shaty Grey" is their target and provides information about her group. The leader of the group tells his comrades that they must work together and they can evenly split the bounty, and makes sure the informant will relay any bit of information to them. He also adds that their employer, Leonardo Hapoon, has friends on the ship, so they must not cause a commotion.

Yor heads to the second-class suite with Olka's group and explains that they are heading to a masquerade ball to blend into the crowd and lose their pursuers. Once at the ball, Yor immediately senses the bloodlust of other assassins and quickly deals with them. As the group head to the shopping promenade, Loid and Anya are also there on their way back to their cabin. Anya spots a skeleton keychain she wants to get and throws a tantrum when Loid refuses. However, Loid, who has noticed listening devices, undercover SSS officers, and suspicious individuals on the ship, starts to overthink his refusal. Suddenly, Anya hears the thoughts of Sickle-and-Chain Barnaby, a rogue assassin who plans on taking the bounty for himself and approaches Olka's group, ready to fight Yor.[6]

Anya realizes she must keep Loid away to protect Yor's identity and tricks him into staying in the souvenir shop to dress as a fun and upbeat father. Anya rushes to Yor, who has begun fighting Barnaby. Yor is scared to see Anya near, but the little girl feigns ignorance and tricks the crowd into thinking that a circus performance is taking place. During their battle, Yor struggles to close the gap and realizes that she is hesitating for some reason. Yor manages to find an opening when Barnaby gets distracted by the crowd and defeats him by tying him up in his own chains and striking his pressure points, immobilizing the assassin. After Yor leaves, Anya heads back to the shop, where Loid has finished dressing up, outfitted in an outlandish combination of clothes and accessories. To his shock, Anya is unimpressed and calls him uncool.[7]

Yor's Doubts[]

The Assassin Leader enters Olka's old cabin to obtain the group's scent, then asks the informant for any leads on Olka's location, to which the man has none. After overhearing other assassins plotting to backstab him, the informant decides to prepare some contingencies. Meanwhile, Loid and Anya head to their room and wonder how Yor is doing.

Yor and the group arrive at their new cabin, where Furseal helps calm down Olka and Gram. Olka asks Furseal, whose true name is Zeb, why he accompanied her. Zeb explains that he owes her and the previous boss and promises to protect her from harm. Matthew arrives and orders Yor to secure the room while he patrols the floor to whittle down the enemy numbers. Before leaving, he warns Yor to stay focused on the job or everyone will die. As Yor keeps watch of the room for the night, she contemplates not being able to contact Loid and Anya and imagines herself with them. Yor realizes that she was hesitating in her fight with Barnaby because she was scared of breaking her cover and leaving her family. After remembering Olka's question if the family is just a cover, Yor thinks about her family—Yuri and the Forgers—and begins having more doubts about her assassin job.[8]

The next day, Franky walks Bond early in the morning in Berlint. Franky is irritated at his current situation, but he quickly changes gears when he realizes he can meet women with Bond, and he proposes that the dog be his pet. Back on the cruise, Loid reflects on his inability to understand Anya the night before and vows to overcome this challenge. Elsewhere, Matthew gives the other city hall group members the day off as he prepares for the next step of Olka's rendezvous. Anya and Loid head out to explore the ship, and Anya plans to ditch Loid so she can help Yor more with her work. Her plan to distract him fails as she gets distracted by the ship's activities for most of the day, much to Anya's distress. Loid sees Anya's displeasure during dinnertime and is concerned for her. Hearing his worried thoughts, Anya explains that she is fine, but she likes it best when the whole family is together. Loid realizes he is overreacting and suggests sending a message to Yor, and adds that they can go to tonight's fireworks show to look for her there.

At the same time, Matthew receives the ready signal from the rendezvous ship and informs Yor, prompting the group to head out in new disguises.[9] The group's plan is to head to a storage room at the fore of the second deck. However, the passageways are guarded by the enemy, as the Assassin Leader had caught on to their scent earlier and sent out the assassins to keep watch. Yor decides to go through the upper deck, where they get startled by the sounds of the fireworks show when it begins. Shortly after, they are quickly ambushed and surrounded by skilled assassins.[10]

Yor sees no escape for them, but Matthew arrives to assist the group. Yor manages to secure Olka and the others inside a hatch and begins her killing spree of the assassins, with the fireworks drowning out the sounds of the violence. Yor finishes off all but a few assassins as Matthew cleans the bloody mess.[11]

The Assassin Leader steps forward and converses with the Garden assassins, distracting them long enough for a Swordsman to land a sneak attack and incapacitate Matthew. Yor fights the Swordsman alone, but gets distracted by her lingering thoughts of her family and doubts about her assassin job, causing her to take a huge disadvantage. Yor gets knocked down and backed into a corner but is still able to stop the Leader from getting to Olka. As her life flashes before her eyes, Yor remembers her reason for becoming an assassin: to protect Yuri's carefree life. Yor wants to prevent tragedies from befalling her brother, and finds it more true than ever now that she has the Forger family. Reinvigorated, Yor gets back up and resumes her fight with the Swordsman. Assured that Loid would respect and understand if she must leave the Forgers because of the dangerous life she lives, Yor is determined to not give up this fight.[1]

Interlude: The Briar Family[]

Meanwhile, in Berlint, Yuri remembers that Yor is away on her trip, which causes his immune system to break down. This takes effect during his job, as he suddenly catches a cold and collapses while chasing a suspect. While he recovers, Yuri flashes back to when he got sick as a child and was cared for by Yor, who eagerly tried to help him get better. As the siblings affirmed how lucky they were to have each other, Yuri wakes up from his memory. The SSS Lieutenant arrives with medicine, and Yuri is keen on resuming his work for Yor's sake after taking it, but the Lieutenant is quick to refuse him.[12]

The Fireworks Finale[]

After leaving the fireworks show, Loid and Anya learn there is a bomb planted inside the ship. Loid decides to intervene while Anya asks to get dropped off at a nearby daycare, though she quickly leaves shortly after to find Yor. After gaining enough intel, Loid arrives at the bomb's location disguised as a crew member so he can disarm it. During her search for Yor, Anya hears the thoughts of the informant, who reveals that Yor is fighting on the roof deck. Anya heads over there and finds Yor's stiletto, which she dropped earlier during her fight with the Swordsman. Anya is able to throw the stiletto up to the deck and incidentally takes out two hitmen. Yor sees and recovers her stiletto, which allows her to defeat the Swordsman with a finishing blow and end the fight. Meanwhile, Loid successfully defuses the bomb, but he begins to suspect that there are more as another in the ship ticks to its countdown.[13]

Yor wonders how she found the stiletto the way she did, prompting Anya to run away from the scene. While Yor checks on Matthew, the injured Assassin Leader also makes his escape. Loid shares his suspicions about there being more bombs with the rest of the crew and suggests evacuating the passengers, but the SSS agents reject him. While the crew sweep the ship for bombs, Anya goes through the upper deck and encounters the Leader, who detects a bomb inside a clock and deduces that it is the work of the informant. Hearing his thoughts, Anya informs a crewman about the clock. Just outside the ship, the Assassin Leader finds the informant, Snoops, attempting to escape on a raft, and confronts him. Snoops reveals that he planted the bombs and made them appear to be from Westalis to incite another war between the East and the West. He then turns on the Leader as he only intended a getaway for himself.

While Loid defuses the other bombs, he is informed of the clock bomb at the upper deck and investigates it. Realizing there is not enough time to defuse it, Loid opts to throw the clock into the sea. Below, Snoops overpowers the Leader and tells him that the "real fireworks show" is about to begin. As this happens, Loid throws the bomb overboard, which detonates above the assassins and knocks them off the raft, leaving them at the mercy of the sharks. Anya watches Loid from afar, but she is found by the daycare worker, who reprimands her for running off and drags her back to the daycare.

Inside the storage area, Yor and Matthew prepare the inflatable boat for Olka and the others' rendezvous. While Matthew gives Zeb instructions, Yor wishes Olka a great life on the other side and receives a hug as thanks. Despite Yor's protests because of her soiled hands, Olka has her hug Gram, saying that Yor's hands are the reason he has a future. Yor appreciates the gesture and embraces the child, remarking how warm he is. Olka then tells Yor that she will pray for her and her family to find peace and happiness.

After Olka leaves, Matthew and Yor watch for the signal from the retrieval ship. Matthew notices Yor getting sentimental and snaps her out of her daze, reminding her that they are soldiers. Despite that, he relays to Yor that Loid and Anya requested to meet her the next day and tells her to accept it as a reward for completing her mission, assuring her that he will be on the lookout for any more killers. Meanwhile, Loid, after managing to secure the ship, returns to the daycare to pick up Anya, and he thinks about how he had to abandon his family again, a thought that gets him to overthink what his mission is.[14]

The Resort Island[]

On the third and final day of the trip, the Forgers reunite at the resort island, where they spend the day together having fun as a family. As she bonds with Loid and Anya, Yor feels at peace, something she wishes could go on forever, which is why she has decided to continue her assassin job. Afterward, the family goes snorkeling and surfing at the sea. At the end of the day, Yor falls asleep on Loid's shoulder, the exhaustion of fighting without rest catching up to her. After Anya does the same, the embarrassed spy is forced to carry the girls back to the ship. Loid notices that Yor must have been working hard but still found time to make Anya's day, which he admires as he tells his wife to rest up. The Forgers return home to a joyful Bond and annoyed Franky, and the family happily sits together over drinks.

Loid later visits Sylvia at the WISE safehouse and briefs her on the bomb incident on the ship, which was not made public by the SSS. Sylvia tells him of several missing passengers who all had fake passports and believes those people may have wanted to instigate a conflict between the East and the West, so she orders Loid to keep an eye out on the extremist movements in Ostania, as it could affect Operation Strix. Sylvia then asks Loid about the vacation, which he tiredly answers was way more work than any other mission as he walks away, which amuses her. Back at home, the rest of the family sleep soundly in the living room, with Anya having drawn a picture of their cruise adventure.[15]

Returning to Eden[]

After the midterm break, Anya returns to school and is ready to impress Becky and Damian about her vacation. However, the wealthy children are unimpressed and brag about their more eventful breaks, causing Anya to embellish the details of her story to get more attention. This backfires as Anya gets ridiculed by her classmates. After classes, Becky tries to cheer up Anya, but George warns her not to lie too much lest she become an outcast like him. Yuri arrives at the Forger apartment, visibly excited to see his sister again. A dejected Anya returns home, and everyone sits in the living room to discuss what happened at school. Loid, Yuri, and Yor ironically advise Anya against lying and to be true to oneself, and Anya decides to stop lying as it seems rough.[16]

After the Cruise: Matthew's Return[]

Shortly after the cruise trip, Matthew goes to Garden HQ to report the mission's completion to the Shopkeeper. The Shopkeeper thanks Matthew and invites him to have dinner together, but Matthew declines to go home instead. He returns home to his wife, Maureen, who is shocked by the bandage on his face. Worried for her husband's safety, she suggests he take up his retirement already, but Matthew states that he wants to keep working as long as "they" want him there. Maureen sighs and decides to cook dinner for Matthew, which he appreciates. As they eat, Matthew compliments Maureen's cooking, which she accepts before asking him for the souvenirs he promised her before his trip.[17]

Story Impact[]

- The assassin organization Garden is introduced.

- The Shopkeeper makes his first physical appearance.

- After rediscovering her reason for becoming an assassin and wanting to protect her new family, Yor chooses to continue her secret assassin job.

title: Manga Milestones 2000-2009: 10 Manga That Changed Comics #1 & #2
author: Admin
date: 2010-01-04
---
There were more manga released each month in 2009 than were released in the entirety of the year 2000. The growth of Japanese-originating comics in the North American comics industry has been phenomenal over the last ten years, with a massive manga boom that never busted (plateaued though), an explosion of material for every gender, every age group, and nearly-every interest. While there are still readers to be initiated and battles to be fought, the preceding decade saw manga arrive in North America; its decades of scouting and waiting paid off in spades for quite a few publishers… and dashed others against the rocks.

There have been thousands of manga released in North America over the past 10 years, but I believe the following 10(-ish) manga were the milestones of the decade, the most important works to be released in English. Depending on how detailed (or long) I wanted this article to go, I could pick 25, 50, 100 manga that serve as milestones, indicative of the industry and the medium and what was and whats to come. But I think I've picked 10 manga that paint the most vivid picture of the medium so I'm going to go with those–part of the fun of making lists like these is seeing where opinions differ, and what's important to the writer (me!).

Spy × Family is a Japanese manga series written and illustrated by Tatsuya Endo. The series began serialization on the manga website Shōnen Jump+ on March 25, 2019. Its individual chapters have been collected in 15 tankōbon volumes, with the first having been released on July 4, 2019. The series is licensed for English-language release in North America by Viz Media, who published the first volume on June 2, 2020. As the series is published in Japan, it is also released simultaneously in English digitally on Viz Media's website.

The covers of the tankōbon features a main character resting on a designer's chair, surrounded by item(s) or characteristics that represent the character, their life and their personalities. The real life chairs were chosen by the author as he deemed fit with the character's personalities. For volume 10, Endo decides to forgo the inclusion of the designer chair motif to make the cover befit the volume's story.

There were more manga released each month in 2009 than were released in the entirety of the year 2000. The growth of Japanese-originating comics in the North American comics industry has been phenomenal over the last ten years, with a massive manga boom that never busted (plateaued though), an explosion of material for every gender, every age group, and nearly-every interest. While there are still readers to be initiated and battles to be fought, the preceding decade saw manga arrive in North America; its decades of scouting and waiting paid off in spades for quite a few publishers… and dashed others against the rocks.

There have been thousands of manga released in North America over the past 10 years, but I believe the following 10(-ish) manga were the milestones of the decade, the most important works to be released in English. Depending on how detailed (or long) I wanted this article to go, I could pick 25, 50, 100 manga that serve as milestones, indicative of the industry and the medium and what was and whats to come. But I think I've picked 10 manga that paint the most vivid picture of the medium so I'm going to go with those–part of the fun of making lists like these is seeing where opinions differ, and what's important to the writer (me!).

Since its inception in 1968, Weekly Shonen Jump has sold over 7.5 billion copies (with weekly circulation exceeding 6.5 million at its height in the 1990s), consistently ranking as the world's most popular comic-book anthology.[1] It remains a particularly important outlet for new manga creators, many of whom—Eiichiro Oda included—developed their skills as assistants for its established creators.

Format

As its title suggests, Weekly Shonen Jump primarily targets the shonen demographic of teenage boys, and trends toward series with majority-male casts and spectacle-heavy plots (though recent polls have indicated several of its series, One Piece included, may actually have majority-female readerships).[2] In addition to One Piece, it has launched some of Japan's most iconic shonen properties, including KochiKame, Dragon Ball, JoJo's Bizarre Adventure, Rurouni Kenshin, Yu-Gi-Oh!, Naruto, Bleach, and My Hero Academia.

Manga, or comics, have appeared in translation in many different languages in different countries. France represents about 40% of the European comic market and in 2011, manga represented 40% of the comics being published in the country. In 2007, 70% of the comics sold in Germany were manga. In the United States, manga comprises a small (but growing) industry, especially when compared to the inroads that Japanese animation or Japanese video games have made in the USA. One example of a manga publisher in the United States, VIZ Media, functions as the American affiliate of the Japanese publishers Shogakukan and Shueisha. ──When did you become Tatsuya Endo's editor?

An original animation DVD (OAD) was bundled and released with the special edition 10th manga volume on December 4, 2015. Manga, or comics, have appeared in translation in many different languages in different countries. France represents about 40% of the European comic market and in 2011, manga represented 40% of the comics being published in the country. In 2007, 70% of the comics sold in Germany were manga. In the United States, manga comprises a small (but growing) industry, especially when compared to the inroads that Japanese animation or Japanese video games have made in the USA. One example of a manga publisher in the United States, VIZ Media, functions as the American affiliate of the Japanese publishers Shogakukan and Shueisha. Though the United Kingdom has some manga publishers like Titan Manga and formerly Tanoshimi most manga sold in the United Kingdom are published by U.S. publishing companies like Viz Media and Kodansha Comics which are in turn owned by their Japanese counterparts. Alongside the United Kingdom, the U.S. manga publishers also sell their English translated manga in other English speaking nations like Canada, Australia and New Zealand with manga being quite popular in Australia compared to other English speaking countries.

There were more manga released each month in 2009 than were released in the entirety of the year 2000. The growth of Japanese-originating comics in the North American comics industry has been phenomenal over the last ten years, with a massive manga boom that never busted (plateaued though), an explosion of material for every gender, every age group, and nearly-every interest. While there are still readers to be initiated and battles to be fought, the preceding decade saw manga arrive in North America; its decades of scouting and waiting paid off in spades for quite a few publishers… and dashed others against the rocks.

There have been thousands of manga released in North America over the past 10 years, but I believe the following 10(-ish) manga were the milestones of the decade, the most important works to be released in English. Depending on how detailed (or long) I wanted this article to go, I could pick 25, 50, 100 manga that serve as milestones, indicative of the industry and the medium and what was and whats to come. But I think I've picked 10 manga that paint the most vivid picture of the medium so I'm going to go with those–part of the fun of making lists like these is seeing where opinions differ, and what's important to the writer (me!).

Manga, or comics, have appeared in translation in many different languages in different countries. France represents about 40% of the European comic market and in 2011, manga represented 40% of the comics being published in the country. In 2007, 70% of the comics sold in Germany were manga. In the United States, manga comprises a small (but growing) industry, especially when compared to the inroads that Japanese animation or Japanese video games have made in the USA. One example of a manga publisher in the United States, VIZ Media, functions as the American affiliate of the Japanese publishers Shogakukan and Shueisha. Though the United Kingdom has some manga publishers like Titan Manga and formerly Tanoshimi most manga sold in the United Kingdom are published by U.S. publishing companies like Viz Media and Kodansha Comics which are in turn owned by their Japanese counterparts. Alongside the United Kingdom, the U.S. manga publishers also sell their English translated manga in other English speaking nations like Canada, Australia and New Zealand with manga being quite popular in Australia compared to other English speaking countries.

There were more manga released each month in 2009 than were released in the entirety of the year 2000. The growth of Japanese-originating comics in the North American comics industry has been phenomenal over the last ten years, with a massive manga boom that never busted (plateaued though), an explosion of material for every gender, every age group, and nearly-every interest. While there are still readers to be initiated and battles to be fought, the preceding decade saw manga arrive in North America; its decades of scouting and waiting paid off in spades for quite a few publishers… and dashed others against the rocks.

There have been thousands of manga released in North America over the past 10 years, but I believe the following 10(-ish) manga were the milestones of the decade, the most important works to be released in English. Depending on how detailed (or long) I wanted this article to go, I could pick 25, 50, 100 manga that serve as milestones, indicative of the industry and the medium and what was and whats to come. But I think I've picked 10 manga that paint the most vivid picture of the medium so I'm going to go with those–part of the fun of making lists like these is seeing where opinions differ, and what's important to the writer (me!).

Chainsaw Man is Tatsuki Fujimoto's most famous ongoing work, although with other acclaimed projects before and since then, including Fire Punch, Goodbye, Eri, and Look Back (recently adapted into a successful anime movie) he's amassed an adoring following. However, Fujimoto's work has not only shaped the readers' perception of his idiosyncratic style over the years, but also the careers of many other mangaka. The Chainsaw Man creator had incredible assistants behind him, including Tatsuya Endo, Oto Tōda, Yuji Kaku, Yukinobu Tatsu, and Tohru Kuramori.

Chainsaw Man has become a global phenomenon, selling over 28 million copies. Fujimoto's many assistants have also gone on to create stories and attain impressive presences in the manga scene, with massive hit anime to many of their credit. author: Admin

There were more manga released each month in 2009 than were released in the entirety of the year 2000. The growth of Japanese-originating comics in the North American comics industry has been phenomenal over the last ten years, with a massive manga boom that never busted (plateaued though), an explosion of material for every gender, every age group, and nearly-every interest. While there are still readers to be initiated and battles to be fought, the preceding decade saw manga arrive in North America; its decades of scouting and waiting paid off in spades for quite a few publishers… and dashed others against the rocks.

There have been thousands of manga released in North America over the past 10 years, but I believe the following 10(-ish) manga were the milestones of the decade, the most important works to be released in English. Depending on how detailed (or long) I wanted this article to go, I could pick 25, 50, 100 manga that serve as milestones, indicative of the industry and the medium and what was and whats to come. But I think I've picked 10 manga that paint the most vivid picture of the medium so I'm going to go with those–part of the fun of making lists like these is seeing where opinions differ, and what's important to the writer (me!).

title: Manga outside Japan - Wikipedia

Manga, or comics, have appeared in translation in many different languages in different countries. France represents about 40% of the European comic market and in 2011, manga represented 40% of the comics being published in the country. In 2007, 70% of the comics sold in Germany were manga. In the United States, manga comprises a small (but growing) industry, especially when compared to the inroads that Japanese animation or Japanese video games have made in the USA. One example of a manga publisher in the United States, VIZ Media, functions as the American affiliate of the Japanese publishers Shogakukan and Shueisha. Though the United Kingdom has some manga publishers like Titan Manga and formerly Tanoshimi most manga sold in the United Kingdom are published by U.S. publishing companies like Viz Media and Kodansha Comics which are in turn owned by their Japanese counterparts. Alongside the United Kingdom, the U.S. manga publishers also sell their English translated manga in other English speaking nations like Canada, Australia and New Zealand with manga being quite popular in Australia compared to other English speaking countries.

Jujutsu Kaisen is undoubtedly one of the most beloved stories in modern Shonen. Even after it has ended, fans continue discussing its characters and story. While the author's narrative choices are debatable, none can disagree that the story has some of the best-written characters in Shonen.

Instead of focusing on well-worn archetypes, the author focuses on creating morally ambiguous and complex characters and provides them with hidden depths and unconventional philosophies that Shonen is not used to seeing.

Itadori Yuji talks to Aoi Todo from Jujutsu Kaisen Season 1 | Credits: Studio Mappa

While they blur the lines between heroism and villainy with a few characters, with a few others, they develop philosophies that are hard to digest. This makes Akutami's characters some of the most complex characters in Shonen.

The Duality of Jujutsu Kaisen's heroes and villains Suguru Geto from Jujutsu Kaisen 0 The Movie | Credits: Studio Mappa

The reliability of Wikipedia and its volunteer-driven and community-regulated editing model, particularly its English-language edition, has been questioned and tested. Wikipedia is written and edited by volunteer editors (known as Wikipedians) who generate online content with the editorial oversight of other volunteer editors via community-generated policies and guidelines. The reliability of the project has been tested statistically through comparative review, analysis of the historical patterns, and strengths and weaknesses inherent in its editing process. The online encyclopedia has been criticized for its factual unreliability, principally regarding its content, presentation, and editorial processes. Studies and surveys attempting to gauge the reliability of Wikipedia have mixed results. Wikipedia's reliability was frequently criticized in the 2000s but has been improved; its English-language edition has been generally praised in the late 2010s and early 2020s.

Select assessments of its reliability have examined how quickly vandalism—content perceived by editors to constitute false or misleading information—is removed. Two years after the project was started, in 2003, an IBM study found that "vandalism is usually repaired extremely quickly—so quickly that most users will never see its effects".Fernanda B. Introduction

What is Wikipedia?

At first pass, it seems like a remarkably simple question with a remarkably simple answer. The average reader knows exactly what Wikipedia is, how to access it and has probably used it on multiple occasions. Almost certainly, if asked, the average reader could explain what Wikipedia is.

Wikipedia is a crowdsourced online encyclopaedia, indeed, the online encyclopaedia. It is one of many projects owned by the Wikimedia Foundation, a non-profit organization based in San Francisco and founded in 2003 to fund Wikipedia (itself launched in 2001) and other such wiki projects, which include media site Wikimedia Commons, dictionary and thesaurus Wiktionary, the knowledge base Wikidata and wikis for books, quotes, travels, a newspaper, tutorials and courses.1 However, Wikipedia is the oldest, largest, and almost certainly best known, of all the Wikimedia projects.

In terms of coverage, usage, currency and public awareness, its nearest online rival, Encyclopaedia Britannica, does not even come close. Encyclopaedia Britannica contains an estimated 120,000 articles;2 as of writing, the English language Wikipedia contains 6,552,009 and rises by roughly 17,000 articles a month.3 How the two compare in terms of perception, accuracy, bias and reliability is another issue entirely, one that has been amply addressed elsewhere.4

How to Cite a Wikipedia Article: MLA, APA, and Chicago Style

Whether writing an essay or completing or scientific lab report, you should cite all primary and secondary sources. Many students include Wikipedia in their digital research. Known as the free encyclopedia, Wikipedia provides information on topics from many categories, including those used in academics.

Although many colleges and universities do not recognize Wikipedia as a reliable source because its pages can be edited by anyone, the site still offers a jumping-off point in several categories of education and literature.

You can use Wikipedia to gather general information or gain a deeper understanding of a topic before delving into a more reputable website, journal, or textbook. Some teachers may allow you to cite Wikipedia as a source if other more reliable references are consulted in addition.

As more students become aware of and rely on the information from Wikipedia, it becomes increasingly important to know how to cite a Wikipedia article properly. Although Wikipedia may not be as revered as other resources, it requires proper citation to use without penalization.

In fact... now it's more true than ever. I don't need to be at peace. I don't care if I have to bloody my hands. Even if it means living a life that could end at any moment... Note that the following sub-headings are fan-made and used to better organize the story.

The Cruise Adventure Arc is the tenth story arc in SPY x FAMILY. In the anime adaptation, the arc is referred as the Luxury Cruise Ship Arc (

The assassin Thorn Princess receives a mission to protect Olka Gretcher and her son from a group of skilled assassins aboard the Princess Lorelei cruise ship. However, when Loid and Anya coincidentally board the same ship thanks to a giveaway they won, Yor begins to have doubts about her life as an assassin.

Summary[]

The Informant's Romance Endeavors[]

Loid visits Franky's store to pick up some items for an extra mission. Loid asks for some pictures he requested, but Franky says his contact that specialized in that intel got done in by Garden, an assassin group in Ostania that takes orders from the shadow government and is believed to be urban legends. Loid still requests the pictures, but Franky wants his help for a job in exchange for the extra trouble: finding a missing cat. Franky explains that the cat, Kopi, belongs to a girl he is trying to court. Completely uninterested, Loid turns him down. Franky turns to his contacts to find Kopi's location, which is near city hall, and on his way there, he runs into Yor, who is out on her lunch break.

After Franky explains his situation, Yor decides to help him out. Franky sets up several of his own inventions to locate Kopi and uses a catnip device to lure in the feline. However, the device draws in a large crowd of cats that swarm Yor and Franky, but Kopi is spotted among them. Franky tries to catch Kopi but fails, and he decides to use his exo-skeleton power suit. But when Kopi starts heading to a major street, Yor tears off a chunk of the exo-skeleton and throws it at the cat, stopping it in its tracks and allowing Yor to capture him. While he lost ten years of his work, Franky returns Kopi only to learn that the girl already has a boyfriend. Yor returns to work at city hall, and Director Matthew McMahon informs Yor that she has a call from her "special contact." Answering the phone, the Thorn Princess receives a new "client."[2]

Thorn Princess's New Assignment[]

Yor and Matthew head to a luxurious garden maintained by the Shopkeeper. Yor and the Shopkeeper briefly chat before the Shopkeeper suddenly attacks her, wanting to test if her skills have dulled. Yor swiftly dodges the attack, and the Shopkeeper comfortably assigns her a new job to protect her client. The Shopkeeper explains that the Gretcher mob family, who have managed Ostania's underworld, has recently lost their patriarch and his sons in an internal dispute, with only his daughter, Olka Gretcher, and her son as the sole survivors. The new leader of the organization, Leonardo Hapoon, has put an enormous bounty on the mother and son's heads that almost every hitman in and out of the country is out for them. Because the Shopkeeper owes a debt to the previous boss, he has chosen to assist Olka, deciding that seeking asylum in a foreign country is her best option. She will do this by fleeing by sea, traveling on a normal passenger ship, and later rendezvous with another at the port of disembarkation.

Yor's assignment is to protect Olka and her son from the assassins and act as a backup in case something goes wrong. Yor is hesitant as she worries about her cover at work and home. However, Garden has already prepared a cover story that she is there as part of her work. With her mind at rest, the Thorn Princess gladly accepts the assignment. On her way home, Yor encounters Yuri, and she begins to wonder with him now grown up and independent of her if there is a point in keeping her assassin job.

Meanwhile, Loid and Anya are at the mall when they see a raffle with a grand prize of two tickets for a three-day, two-night cruise on a ship named Princess Lorelei, which sails through the islands in Ostanian coastal waters. Excited, Anya is determined to go on the trip and participates in the raffle. She soon realizes that the host has rigged the raffle for himself, so she takes the winning tickets. When Yor returns home, Anya shows her the tickets, and Loid suggests that Yor and Anya go on the cruise together since he has work. However, Yor recognizes it as the same ship she will be on for her job. Anya reads her mind and, after some thought, insists on going on the trip. Loid then goes to Sylvia to ask for time off, and, to his surprise, she allows him to go and tells him to consider the trip as part of Anya's care and education for Operation Strix, treating it like any other mission.

On the Friday of the departure, the Forgers head to the port, leaving Bond at home with Franky. On their way there, Yor wishes she could spend her time with Loid and Anya, and wonders if she could make this trip her final job as the Thorn Princess. Upon reaching Princess Lorelei, the family split up as suspicious figures also board the ship.[3]

The Assassin Ambush[]

Inside Princess Lorelei, Anya is amazed by the many activities the boat offers, but not so much for their third-class suite. Meanwhile, Yor and the city hall group meet with Olka, who has disguised herself as "Shaty Grey," alongside her ally and acting husband, "Furseal." As the rest of the group tours around the ship, Yor stays behind with Olka. The women talk, and Yor learns about Olka's desire to live a quiet life with her son, away from power and money. Olka requests to go outside for a moment, but Yor is reluctant since Loid and Anya are also on the ship. On the lower suite, Loid and Anya explore the ship. Loid finds himself falling back to "Twilight mode" and is determined to attain optimal recreation.

Yor explains her family situation to Olka, who questions if the family really is just for her cover. Olka lends Yor her clothes as a disguise, and they head outside with Olka's son. Yor empathizes with Olka's circumstances and promises to finish the job without fail. Touched, Olka reveals her son's name to Yor, Gram. Their conversation is heard on a listening device, and an informant uses this information to locate Olka's cabin room.[4]

At nighttime, Yor's co-workers have dinner at a pub and talk about Yor's trip. On the ship, the city hall group and the Grey family eat at a fancy restaurant. Afterward, the men leave for a bar while Yor and Olka head back to the cabin. There, Olka notes there has not been any sign of trouble the entire day, but Yor warns her that they must keep their guard up as they have no idea where the enemy is or what their plan is. She predicts that the enemy will try attacking at the last possible minute, which will be the next day. Olka asks what everyone else will do if she manages to escape safely, and Yor explains their prepared cover story. Olka then asks if Yor will see her family after she completes her mission, as the ship will stop at a resort island on the third day. She suggests that Yor could use it to spend time with her family, but Yor is unsure.

On the lower deck, Loid and Anya have their dinner and take note of how strange it is to have dinner without Yor, which leads to Loid getting embarrassed when Anya calls him sappy for missing Yor. Meanwhile, after leaving the bar with the other men, Matthew notices they are being followed. He ambushes their stalker and interrogates him for information. Upon learning there are many assassins on board the ship and know Olka's location, Matthew grabs Furseal and rushes back to her cabin, realizing that the enemy had no intention of waiting.

At the cabin, the women hear someone knock on the door.[5] Behind it is an assassin who immediately attacks, but Yor kills him shortly after Matthew and Furseal arrive. Matthew brings everyone up to speed with their situation and orders Yor to take the others to another cabin in the second-class suite, but not before giving everyone masks to disguise themselves. The informant from earlier informs a group of assassins that "Shaty Grey" is their target and provides information about her group. The leader of the group tells his comrades that they must work together and they can evenly split the bounty, and makes sure the informant will relay any bit of information to them. He also adds that their employer, Leonardo Hapoon, has friends on the ship, so they must not cause a commotion.

Yor heads to the second-class suite with Olka's group and explains that they are heading to a masquerade ball to blend into the crowd and lose their pursuers. Once at the ball, Yor immediately senses the bloodlust of other assassins and quickly deals with them. As the group head to the shopping promenade, Loid and Anya are also there on their way back to their cabin. Anya spots a skeleton keychain she wants to get and throws a tantrum when Loid refuses. However, Loid, who has noticed listening devices, undercover SSS officers, and suspicious individuals on the ship, starts to overthink his refusal. Suddenly, Anya hears the thoughts of Sickle-and-Chain Barnaby, a rogue assassin who plans on taking the bounty for himself and approaches Olka's group, ready to fight Yor.[6]

Anya realizes she must keep Loid away to protect Yor's identity and tricks him into staying in the souvenir shop to dress as a fun and upbeat father. Anya rushes to Yor, who has begun fighting Barnaby. Yor is scared to see Anya near, but the little girl feigns ignorance and tricks the crowd into thinking that a circus performance is taking place. During their battle, Yor struggles to close the gap and realizes that she is hesitating for some reason. Yor manages to find an opening when Barnaby gets distracted by the crowd and defeats him by tying him up in his own chains and striking his pressure points, immobilizing the assassin. After Yor leaves, Anya heads back to the shop, where Loid has finished dressing up, outfitted in an outlandish combination of clothes and accessories. To his shock, Anya is unimpressed and calls him uncool.[7]

Yor's Doubts[]

The Assassin Leader enters Olka's old cabin to obtain the group's scent, then asks the informant for any leads on Olka's location, to which the man has none. After overhearing other assassins plotting to backstab him, the informant decides to prepare some contingencies. Meanwhile, Loid and Anya head to their room and wonder how Yor is doing.

Yor and the group arrive at their new cabin, where Furseal helps calm down Olka and Gram. Olka asks Furseal, whose true name is Zeb, why he accompanied her. Zeb explains that he owes her and the previous boss and promises to protect her from harm. Matthew arrives and orders Yor to secure the room while he patrols the floor to whittle down the enemy numbers. Before leaving, he warns Yor to stay focused on the job or everyone will die. As Yor keeps watch of the room for the night, she contemplates not being able to contact Loid and Anya and imagines herself with them. Yor realizes that she was hesitating in her fight with Barnaby because she was scared of breaking her cover and leaving her family. After remembering Olka's question if the family is just a cover, Yor thinks about her family—Yuri and the Forgers—and begins having more doubts about her assassin job.[8]

The next day, Franky walks Bond early in the morning in Berlint. Franky is irritated at his current situation, but he quickly changes gears when he realizes he can meet women with Bond, and he proposes that the dog be his pet. Back on the cruise, Loid reflects on his inability to understand Anya the night before and vows to overcome this challenge. Elsewhere, Matthew gives the other city hall group members the day off as he prepares for the next step of Olka's rendezvous. Anya and Loid head out to explore the ship, and Anya plans to ditch Loid so she can help Yor more with her work. Her plan to distract him fails as she gets distracted by the ship's activities for most of the day, much to Anya's distress. Loid sees Anya's displeasure during dinnertime and is concerned for her. Hearing his worried thoughts, Anya explains that she is fine, but she likes it best when the whole family is together. Loid realizes he is overreacting and suggests sending a message to Yor, and adds that they can go to tonight's fireworks show to look for her there.

At the same time, Matthew receives the ready signal from the rendezvous ship and informs Yor, prompting the group to head out in new disguises.[9] The group's plan is to head to a storage room at the fore of the second deck. However, the passageways are guarded by the enemy, as the Assassin Leader had caught on to their scent earlier and sent out the assassins to keep watch. Yor decides to go through the upper deck, where they get startled by the sounds of the fireworks show when it begins. Shortly after, they are quickly ambushed and surrounded by skilled assassins.[10]

Yor sees no escape for them, but Matthew arrives to assist the group. Yor manages to secure Olka and the others inside a hatch and begins her killing spree of the assassins, with the fireworks drowning out the sounds of the violence. Yor finishes off all but a few assassins as Matthew cleans the bloody mess.[11]

The Assassin Leader steps forward and converses with the Garden assassins, distracting them long enough for a Swordsman to land a sneak attack and incapacitate Matthew. Yor fights the Swordsman alone, but gets distracted by her lingering thoughts of her family and doubts about her assassin job, causing her to take a huge disadvantage. Yor gets knocked down and backed into a corner but is still able to stop the Leader from getting to Olka. As her life flashes before her eyes, Yor remembers her reason for becoming an assassin: to protect Yuri's carefree life. Yor wants to prevent tragedies from befalling her brother, and finds it more true than ever now that she has the Forger family. Reinvigorated, Yor gets back up and resumes her fight with the Swordsman. Assured that Loid would respect and understand if she must leave the Forgers because of the dangerous life she lives, Yor is determined to not give up this fight.[1]

Interlude: The Briar Family[]

Meanwhile, in Berlint, Yuri remembers that Yor is away on her trip, which causes his immune system to break down. This takes effect during his job, as he suddenly catches a cold and collapses while chasing a suspect. While he recovers, Yuri flashes back to when he got sick as a child and was cared for by Yor, who eagerly tried to help him get better. As the siblings affirmed how lucky they were to have each other, Yuri wakes up from his memory. The SSS Lieutenant arrives with medicine, and Yuri is keen on resuming his work for Yor's sake after taking it, but the Lieutenant is quick to refuse him.[12]

The Fireworks Finale[]

After leaving the fireworks show, Loid and Anya learn there is a bomb planted inside the ship. Loid decides to intervene while Anya asks to get dropped off at a nearby daycare, though she quickly leaves shortly after to find Yor. After gaining enough intel, Loid arrives at the bomb's location disguised as a crew member so he can disarm it. During her search for Yor, Anya hears the thoughts of the informant, who reveals that Yor is fighting on the roof deck. Anya heads over there and finds Yor's stiletto, which she dropped earlier during her fight with the Swordsman. Anya is able to throw the stiletto up to the deck and incidentally takes out two hitmen. Yor sees and recovers her stiletto, which allows her to defeat the Swordsman with a finishing blow and end the fight. Meanwhile, Loid successfully defuses the bomb, but he begins to suspect that there are more as another in the ship ticks to its countdown.[13]

Yor wonders how she found the stiletto the way she did, prompting Anya to run away from the scene. While Yor checks on Matthew, the injured Assassin Leader also makes his escape. Loid shares his suspicions about there being more bombs with the rest of the crew and suggests evacuating the passengers, but the SSS agents reject him. While the crew sweep the ship for bombs, Anya goes through the upper deck and encounters the Leader, who detects a bomb inside a clock and deduces that it is the work of the informant. Hearing his thoughts, Anya informs a crewman about the clock. Just outside the ship, the Assassin Leader finds the informant, Snoops, attempting to escape on a raft, and confronts him. Snoops reveals that he planted the bombs and made them appear to be from Westalis to incite another war between the East and the West. He then turns on the Leader as he only intended a getaway for himself.

While Loid defuses the other bombs, he is informed of the clock bomb at the upper deck and investigates it. Realizing there is not enough time to defuse it, Loid opts to throw the clock into the sea. Below, Snoops overpowers the Leader and tells him that the "real fireworks show" is about to begin. As this happens, Loid throws the bomb overboard, which detonates above the assassins and knocks them off the raft, leaving them at the mercy of the sharks. Anya watches Loid from afar, but she is found by the daycare worker, who reprimands her for running off and drags her back to the daycare.

Inside the storage area, Yor and Matthew prepare the inflatable boat for Olka and the others' rendezvous. While Matthew gives Zeb instructions, Yor wishes Olka a great life on the other side and receives a hug as thanks. Despite Yor's protests because of her soiled hands, Olka has her hug Gram, saying that Yor's hands are the reason he has a future. Yor appreciates the gesture and embraces the child, remarking how warm he is. Olka then tells Yor that she will pray for her and her family to find peace and happiness.

After Olka leaves, Matthew and Yor watch for the signal from the retrieval ship. Matthew notices Yor getting sentimental and snaps her out of her daze, reminding her that they are soldiers. Despite that, he relays to Yor that Loid and Anya requested to meet her the next day and tells her to accept it as a reward for completing her mission, assuring her that he will be on the lookout for any more killers. Meanwhile, Loid, after managing to secure the ship, returns to the daycare to pick up Anya, and he thinks about how he had to abandon his family again, a thought that gets him to overthink what his mission is.[14]

The Resort Island[]

On the third and final day of the trip, the Forgers reunite at the resort island, where they spend the day together having fun as a family. As she bonds with Loid and Anya, Yor feels at peace, something she wishes could go on forever, which is why she has decided to continue her assassin job. Afterward, the family goes snorkeling and surfing at the sea. At the end of the day, Yor falls asleep on Loid's shoulder, the exhaustion of fighting without rest catching up to her. After Anya does the same, the embarrassed spy is forced to carry the girls back to the ship. Loid notices that Yor must have been working hard but still found time to make Anya's day, which he admires as he tells his wife to rest up. The Forgers return home to a joyful Bond and annoyed Franky, and the family happily sits together over drinks.

Loid later visits Sylvia at the WISE safehouse and briefs her on the bomb incident on the ship, which was not made public by the SSS. Sylvia tells him of several missing passengers who all had fake passports and believes those people may have wanted to instigate a conflict between the East and the West, so she orders Loid to keep an eye out on the extremist movements in Ostania, as it could affect Operation Strix. Sylvia then asks Loid about the vacation, which he tiredly answers was way more work than any other mission as he walks away, which amuses her. Back at home, the rest of the family sleep soundly in the living room, with Anya having drawn a picture of their cruise adventure.[15]

Returning to Eden[]

After the midterm break, Anya returns to school and is ready to impress Becky and Damian about her vacation. However, the wealthy children are unimpressed and brag about their more eventful breaks, causing Anya to embellish the details of her story to get more attention. This backfires as Anya gets ridiculed by her classmates. After classes, Becky tries to cheer up Anya, but George warns her not to lie too much lest she become an outcast like him. Yuri arrives at the Forger apartment, visibly excited to see his sister again. A dejected Anya returns home, and everyone sits in the living room to discuss what happened at school. Loid, Yuri, and Yor ironically advise Anya against lying and to be true to oneself, and Anya decides to stop lying as it seems rough.[16]

After the Cruise: Matthew's Return[]

Shortly after the cruise trip, Matthew goes to Garden HQ to report the mission's completion to the Shopkeeper. The Shopkeeper thanks Matthew and invites him to have dinner together, but Matthew declines to go home instead. He returns home to his wife, Maureen, who is shocked by the bandage on his face. Worried for her husband's safety, she suggests he take up his retirement already, but Matthew states that he wants to keep working as long as "they" want him there. Maureen sighs and decides to cook dinner for Matthew, which he appreciates. As they eat, Matthew compliments Maureen's cooking, which she accepts before asking him for the souvenirs he promised her before his trip.[17]

Story Impact[]

- The assassin organization Garden is introduced.

- The Shopkeeper makes his first physical appearance.

- After rediscovering her reason for becoming an assassin and wanting to protect her new family, Yor chooses to continue her secret assassin job.

Personality[]

Endo aspired to be a manga artist since childhood. His family consists of one parent and one elder brother. His favorite actors are Bruce Lee and Hiroshi Abe, and his favorite actresses are Meg Ryan and Audrey Tautou. His favorite manga artists are Akira Toriyama, Hiroyuki Nishimori, and Minetaro Mochizuki. His hobbies, special skills, pride include skiing, basketball, racket-based ball games, repeated side-steps, doing nothing, getting stomatitis, and health destruction.[1]

Career[]

These anime series have been shown and have achieved varying levels of popularity in the United States and Canada, this is contributed to the era known as the "anime boom" which lasted from the mid-1990s to mid-2000s. In the United States, most anime can be seen televised on channels, with channels such as Adult Swim's Toonami block, and Toku airing anime targeted toward young adults to adult audiences, and with channels such as Disney XD, and Nicktoons airing anime targeted toward children audiences. Anime can also be viewed online legally on streaming websites such as Anime Network, Funimation's FunimationNow platform, Crunchyroll, Netflix, Crackle, YouTube, HBO Max and Hulu.

1960s[]

In the 1960s, Astro Boy, Speed Racer and Kimba the White Lion were introduced to the US and were received positively. However audiences didn't see them as Japanese, possibly because they resembled most American cartoons of the time. If you were an anime fan in America at the time you would have to rely on fansubs.[1]

Manga, or comics, have appeared in translation in many different languages in different countries. France represents about 40% of the European comic market and in 2011, manga represented 40% of the comics being published in the country. In 2007, 70% of the comics sold in Germany were manga. In the United States, manga comprises a small (but growing) industry, especially when compared to the inroads that Japanese animation or Japanese video games have made in the USA. One example of a manga publisher in the United States, VIZ Media, functions as the American affiliate of the Japanese publishers Shogakukan and Shueisha. Though the United Kingdom has some manga publishers like Titan Manga and formerly Tanoshimi most manga sold in the United Kingdom are published by U.S. publishing companies like Viz Media and Kodansha Comics which are in turn owned by their Japanese counterparts. Alongside the United Kingdom, the U.S. manga publishers also sell their English translated manga in other English speaking nations like Canada, Australia and New Zealand with manga being quite popular in Australia compared to other English speaking countries.

Weekly Shonen Jump (週刊少年ジャンプ, Shūkan Shōnen Janpu?, commonly stylized as Weekly Jump or simply Jump in English) is a weekly manga magazine published by Shueisha. It is responsible for serializing the One Piece manga—among many others—in its original, single-chapter form.

Since its inception in 1968, Weekly Shonen Jump has sold over 7.5 billion copies (with weekly circulation exceeding 6.5 million at its height in the 1990s), consistently ranking as the world's most popular comic-book anthology.[1] It remains a particularly important outlet for new manga creators, many of whom—Eiichiro Oda included—developed their skills as assistants for its established creators.

Format

As its title suggests, Weekly Shonen Jump primarily targets the shonen demographic of teenage boys, and trends toward series with majority-male casts and spectacle-heavy plots (though recent polls have indicated several of its series, One Piece included, may actually have majority-female readerships).[2] In addition to One Piece, it has launched some of Japan's most iconic shonen properties, including KochiKame, Dragon Ball, JoJo's Bizarre Adventure, Rurouni Kenshin, Yu-Gi-Oh!, Naruto, Bleach, and My Hero Academia.

Spy × Family is a Japanese manga series written and illustrated by Tatsuya Endo. The series began serialization on the manga website Shōnen Jump+ on March 25, 2019. Its individual chapters have been collected in 15 tankōbon volumes, with the first having been released on July 4, 2019. The series is licensed for English-language release in North America by Viz Media, who published the first volume on June 2, 2020. The covers of the tankōbon features a main character resting on a designer's chair, surrounded by item(s) or characteristics that represent the character, their life and their personalities. The real life chairs were chosen by the author as he deemed fit with the character's personalities. For volume 10, Endo decides to forgo the inclusion of the designer chair motif to make the cover befit the volume's story.

Underpinning the massively popular anime industry is an even more popular industry that feeds it—Japanese graphic novels, commonly known as manga. And manga is hotter than ever.

Action-fantasy powerhouse Demon Slayer, animal romance Beastars and comedy series Spy X Family all originated as manga. And while it has been massively successful in foreign markets for nearly two decades, manga is really flourishing in North America right now, with US based publishers such as VIZ Media and Square Enix Manga reporting that sales in the region have more than doubled in the last two years.

Manga is now the number-one graphic novel format in North America, beating the likes of Marvel and DC Comics on their home turf. In a February 2022 report, the NPD Group noted that manga was responsible for one-quarter of all growth in the US book market in 2021, and the publishing category's annual sales were up by US$218 million year over year.

Several factors are at play that have helped Japanese graphic novels skyrocket to these new heights, according to Masaaki Shimizu, GM and publisher of Square Enix's manga and books imprint.
